findings.evidence: CayleyPath.lean:283 `def cayleyPath` builds on `cayleyPathEnd`, and `cayleyPathEnd_eq` is `cayleyPathFormula (smoothTransition t) (J₀.toEndomorphism x) (J₁.toEndomorphism x)`, which is exactly the `toEndomorphism` of `tameCayleyPath` (TameCayleyPath.lean:122-124).
findings.fix: Generalize `cayleyPath` to take `h₁ : σ.Tames J₁`, defined as this PR's `tameCayleyPath` body. Keep `compatible_cayleyPath (h₁' : σ.Compatible J₁)` as the one compatible-specific lemma. Delete `tameCayleyPath`, `tameCayleyPath_eq_cayleyPath` and the private `cayleyPathEnd*` helpers, and update `SeamFamily.lean` call sites to pass `h.tames`.
findings.issue: `SmoothTwoForm.Compatible.tameCayleyPath` duplicates the existing `SmoothTwoForm.Compatible.cayleyPath` (CayleyPath.lean:283). Its compatible-endpoint case equals `cayleyPath` (`tameCayleyPath_eq_cayleyPath`), and `cayleyPath` uses `h₁` only through `.tames` (`contMDiff_cayleyPathEnd` now calls `h₀.contMDiff_cayleyPathFormula h₁.tames`).

findings.evidence: Statements are identical up to `Compatible` vs `Tames` on `J₁`. `contMDiff_cayleyPath_family` is `contMDiff_cayleyPathEnd_family`, which the PR reduces to `contMDiff_cayleyPathFormula_family hc₀ (fun p ↦ (hc₁ p).tames)`.

findings.evidence: Smooth.lean:359-361 `cayleyPath := h₀.cayleyInterp h₁ ⟨smoothTransition.nonneg t, …⟩` and the new def at 432-436 both send `smoothTransition t • J₀.cayley J₁` through the inverse Cayley chart. `cayleyEquiv` and `compatibleCayleyEquiv` agree on the compatible ball, which `cayleyPath_eq_compatibleCayleyEquiv_symm` (364) and `compatibleCayleyContraction_eq` (Contractible.lean:181) already rely on.

Keep `compatible_cayleyPath` with an extra `ω.Compatible J₁` hypothesis, proved via `cayley_mem_compatibleCayleyBall_iff` as in `compatible_cayleyContraction` (Contractible.lean:153). Prove `contDiff_cayleyPath` and `cayleyPath_eq_compatibleCayleyEquiv_symm` for the compatible case from that. Delete the `tameCayleyPath` copies.
findings.issue: The linear `SymplecticForm.Compatible.tameCayleyPath` and its lemmas `tames_`, `cayley_`, `_of_nonpos`, `_of_one_le`, `_self` and `toContinuousLinearMap_tameCayleyPath` duplicate `Compatible.cayleyPath` (359), `cayley_cayleyPath` (390), `cayleyPath_of_nonpos`/`_of_one_le` (402-412), `cayleyPath_self` (396) and `toContinuousLinearMap_cayleyPath`. They are the same chart inverse at `smoothTransition t • J₀.cayley J₁`.

summary: The PR adds `tameCayleyPath` (smooth and linear) as a parallel API to the existing `cayleyPath`, which needs only tameness of `J₁` and which the PR itself proves equal to the new path; generalize the existing path instead of duplicating its collar, self, smoothness and family lemmas.
